stories.title: Rahul Gandhi’s Manusmriti Remark Sparks BJP-Congress War Over Women’s Rights
stories.summary: A fresh political battle has erupted between the Congress and BJP over women’s dignity, patriarchy and the Manusmriti. Speaking at Congress’s youth outreach programme in Pune, Rahul Gandhi criticised the Manusmriti’s traditional prescriptions on women and accused the BJP and RSS of promoting a “Manusmriti mindset”. He urged young women to “smash patriarchy” and asserted that women are individuals, not property. The BJP has hit back, accusing Rahul Gandhi of hypocrisy over women’s representation and questioning his stance on the Women’s Reservation Bill. BJP leader Smriti Irani also pointed to the absence of women ministers in the Congress-led Karnataka cabinet. What began as Rahul’s call to challenge patriarchy has now turned into another sharp Congress-BJP political face-off.

stories.title: Earthquake of magnitude 3.5 strikes Leh
stories.summary: Leh , August 24 : An earthquake of magnitude 3.5 struck Ladakh's capital, Leh, early Monday morning, reported the National Centre for Seismology (NCS). Sharing details in a post on X, the seismic monitoring agency stated that the tremor occurred at a depth of 120 km at 8:25 AM Indian Standard Time (IST). "EQ of M: 3.5, On: 24/08/2026 08:25:07 IST, Lat: 36.700 N, Long: 74.343 E, Depth: 120 Km, Location: Leh, Ladakh," the post read. Hours before the Leh earthquake, Himachal Pradesh's Chamba district was also hit by a mild earthquake of magnitude 3.0 at 3:40 AM on Monday. Providing details about the Chamba quake, the NCS posted, "EQ of M: 3.0, On: 24/08/2026 03:40:19 IST, Lat: 32.925 N, Long: 76.145 E, Depth: 8 Km, Location: Chamba, Himachal Pradesh." Earlier, an earthquake measuring 4.6 on the Richter scale struck the Leh region on Sunday. According to the NCS, Sunday's tremor was recorded at a depth of 150 km at 3:34 PM IST. "EQ of M: 4.6, On: 23/08/2026 15:34:42 IST, Lat: 36.736 N, Long: 74.372 E, Depth: 150 Km, Location: Leh Ladakh, Ladakh," the post read. (ANI)

article_sentences: NAZIRA: The devastating flood that hit the region on July 19 not only destroyed the livelihoods of numerous families but also caused extensive damage to several institutions, particularly those in the health sector.
The Khelua Primary Health Centre (PHC), along with the office of the Sub-Divisional Medical Officer at Khelua in Sivasagar district, suffered significant damage in the flood.
As a result, residents of a large area covering the Betbari and Haschara mouzas are facing considerable difficulties in accessing medical treatment and diagnostic services.
Floodwater reportedly rose to nearly four feet inside the health centre and remained there for several days, damaging a large number of essential items and equipment.
A substantial quantity of medicines stored at the facility was also reportedly destroyed.
Laboratory equipment, inverters, refrigerators and electrical appliances were damaged, while sections of the concrete walls of the health centre also suffered considerable damage.
The flood also affected the healthcare network under Khelua PHC.
Of the 19 sub-health centres under its jurisdiction, 16 were reportedly damaged by floodwaters, while only three escaped major damage.
Doctors, nurses and other staff of Khelua PHC have been working to clean the premises and salvage and restore whatever equipment remains usable.
However, local residents believe that the restoration process cannot be completed without adequate support and attention from senior Health Department officials.

With healthcare services severely affected, residents of the surrounding areas have appealed to elected representatives and senior Health Department authorities to take immediate steps to restore Khelua PHC and its sub-health centres.
They urged the authorities to ensure that essential medical services are restored at the earliest and that a safe and healthy healthcare environment is provided for the flood-affected population.

stories.title: Guwahati: Fight against flood hits roadblock of unplanned growth, drainage gaps

article_sentences: GUWAHATI: Guwahati’s recurring urban flooding has exposed gaps in the city’s drainage planning, with rapid construction, expanding transport infrastructure and overlapping departmental responsibilities complicating efforts to build a flood-resilient urban system.

The Assam Government has asked consultants to revise the proposed Comprehensive Drainage Master Plan for Guwahati and the Detailed Project Report for the Bahini-Bharalu Basin to identify shortcomings and strengthen measures against chronic waterlogging.

Reports in Dispur said the problem extended beyond the capacity of individual drains, as the city’s rapid expansion through flyovers, roads, residential complexes and commercial projects had altered natural water-flow patterns in several areas.
Guwahati has 24 flyovers and bridges either operational or forming part of its expanding transport network.
While these projects have improved connectivity, questions remain over whether adequate storm-water drainage provisions were incorporated into their planning.

The city’s location along the Brahmaputra and its network of natural channels and tributaries has historically allowed wetlands, low-lying areas and drainage channels to absorb and carry excess rainwater.
Rapid urbanisation and encroachment, however, have placed increasing pressure on these systems.

A senior PWD official also pointed to overlapping responsibilities among agencies, including the Public Works Department, Guwahati Municipal Corporation and other urban bodies, in constructing and maintaining roads and drains.
Changes in desiltation responsibilities have also contributed to uncertainty over the agency responsible for specific stretches.
“There has to be a construction plan and maintenance plan, which is missing in Guwahati,” the official said.
Urban planners and civic experts have called for an integrated drainage map with clearly defined drainage hierarchies, maintenance responsibilities and standard operating procedures.

They have also stressed coordination among the GMC, PWD, GMDA and other agencies, along with separation of storm-water and sewage networks, protection of wetlands and natural channels, action against encroachment and mandatory drainage provisions in major infrastructure projects.

stories.title: Supreme Court Restores Congress Leaders Petition Challenging BJP MP's Election From Assam

article_sentences: The Supreme Court today (August 24) restored an election petition filed by advocate and Indian National Congress member Hafiz Rashid Ahmed Choudhury, challenging the election of Bharatiya Janata Party's Kripanath Mallah, who won the Lok Sabha elections from the No. 7 Karimganj Parliamentary Constituency in Assam during the 2024 General Elections.

A bench comprising Justice JB Pardiwala and Justice K Vinod Chandran allowed the civil appeal, which has been preferred under Section 116A of the Representation of the People Act, 1951, challenging the Gauhati High Court's judgment dated April 4, 2025, which rejected the election petition at the threshold.

By the said judgment, the High Court had dismissed the election petition filed by Choudhary challenging the election of Kripanath, alleging corrupt practices within the meaning of Section 123 of the RP Act.

However, the returned candidate filed an application under Section 86, read with Sections 81 and 83 of the RoP Act, and Section 151 CPC, seeking the outright dismissal of the election petition at the threshold, without going into a full trial.
This was allowed by the High Court.
Choudhury had contested the 2024 parliamentary election from the Karimganj Parliamentary Constituency.
As recorded in the appeal papers, the appellant had secured 5,26,733 votes, while the returned candidate had secured 5,45,093 votes, the difference being 18,360 votes.
Justice Chandran pronounced the judgment as: "Relying on the earlier Constitution Bench judgment, we have allowed the appeal."
Detailed judgment awaited.

stories.title: MNRE Offers Force Majeure Relief to Renewable Projects Hit by West Asia Crisis
stories.summary: The Ministry of New and Renewable Energy (MNRE) has recently issued an advisory to grant a time extension to renewable energy projects affected by Force Majeure. It advised Renewable Energy Implementing Agencies (REIAs) and States/UTs after receiving various representations seeking a time extension and other reliefs due to the ongoing West Asia crisis. The advisory is granted in line with the provisions and procedures for seeking relief under the Force Majeure provisions in the PPA. They granted this extension to projects whose SCSD/SCD or extended SCSD/SCD falls on or after February 28, 2026, for a period of up to four months. MNRE's latest advisory extends to Renewable Energy Implementing Agencies (REIAs), namely Solar Energy Corporation of India Limited ( SEC I), NTPC Limited, NHPC Limited and SJVN Limited, as well as Power/Energy/Renewable Energy Departments of State/UT Governments and organisations/agencies thereunder. I n line with the provision, the Ministry has notified that Force Majeure provisions in the Power Purchase Agreements ( PPAs ) and as per the contractual provisions and procedure, the REIAs/the concerned RE power procuring agencies/entities may consider granting a time extension in the Scheduled Commencement of Supply Date (SCSD)/Scheduled Commissioning Date (SCD) for such renewable energy (RE) power projects. Background Initially, MNRE received representations regarding the issue based on the rising West Asia crisis and issued notices on April 29, 2026, and later on July 6, 2026. In the recent request, developers had sought a time extension for the implementation of their renewable power projects, citing delays in implementation due to disruptions caused by the situation in West Asia. Subsequently, after receiving representations, MNRE also received a request seeking a blanket extension of project timelines for affected renewable energy projects, citing an advisory issued by the Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs (MoHUA). The issue was further taken up on April 29, 2026, by the Department of Expenditure, Ministry of Finance, with the regulatory authorities indicating that an advisory should be issued. In response to this, the Department of Expenditure, Ministry of Finance, clarified that the West Asia situation should be treated as a war and provided for a time extension of up to four months on account of the West Asia situation.

stories.headline: The Growing Complexity of Renewable Energy Insurance: Managing Risks in India's Clean Energy
stories.title: The Growing Complexity of Renewable Energy Insurance: Managing Risks in India's Clean Energy
stories.summary: India's journey towards renewable energy has entered a pivotal phase, where addressing risks has become crucial. By June 2026, the nation had achieved an impressive 288.6 GW of renewable capacity, with solar contributing 162.2 GW and wind 57.4 GW. This milestone not only surpasses its goal of 50% non-fossil power by 2030 but also highlights the country's commitment to a sustainable future, as reported by the Ministry of New and Renewable However, a report from Zurich Resilience Solutions in July 2026 raised some alarms. It indicated that 90% of planned renewable projects across 871 sites might face significant climate risks by 2030 The encouraging part is that with targeted resilience measures, these potential climate-related losses could drop from $55 billion to $27 billion. This is a critical juncture for India to bolster its renewable energy initiatives and ensure they are robust against looming challenges. The insurance landscape is evolving as well. It is no longer just about safeguarding solar panels, wind turbines, or construction equipment from physical damage. As renewable projects expand in size and become more interconnected, they are increasingly vulnerable to climate events. A single cyclone, flood, or hailstorm can impact numerous assets, contractors, and transmission links in the same region, creating accumulation risks for insurers and potentially amplifying losses for developers. This evolving risk scenario is significant because renewable infrastructure is built around delicate project economics. A lengthy outage is not simply a matter of repair costs; it can lead to lost energy generation, delayed debt repayments, and renegotiated contracts. Thus, the conversation around insurance needs to transition from merely protecting assets to safeguarding the very economics of these projects. “Climate exposure starts before construction.” It is vital to recognise that climate exposure can begin long before construction starts. The most impactful insurance decisions are often made before securing a policy. Site selection, drainage design, equipment elevation, and even fire protection plays critical roles in shaping a project's risk profile. The recent Zurich assessment underscores that resilience can substantially alter how climate risks are viewed economically. For developers, this means integrating climate risk analysis into the early stages of engineering and financing. For brokers, it requires ensuring that risk information reaches underwriters in a way that mirrors the actual design and operating environment of each project. Improved information flow can differentiate between risks that are broadly imprecise and those that are well-understood. “New technologies are creating new underwriting questions .” India's renewable energy landscape is becoming more technology-driven, introducing new underwriting challenges. As battery energy storage systems gain importance alongside solar and wind resources, they also bring forth risks that traditional power policies were not designed to cover. Issues like thermal events, system integration failures, and long-term performance concerns necessitate more specialized underwriting approaches. Additionally, the rise of digital monitoring and remote controls adds layers of complexity, exposing assets to cyber risks in an industry historically focused on physical challenges. As a result, insurers cannot depend solely on historical claims data when many of the technologies currently deployed are new. Underwriting will increasingly hinge on engineering data, technology standards, operating procedures, and the quality of risk management. “Insurance must become part of project architecture.” To support India’s clean energy ambitions, insurance needs to evolve beyond a mere financial requirement to a form of risk intelligence. Brokers play a crucial role in this transformation, needing to distil intricate engineering and climate data into insurance structures that work financially, while also helping developers identify opportunities to mitigate risks rather than exclusively transferring them. This shift opens avenues for more advanced solutions, including coverage linked to business interruption, performance, and, where applicable, measurable weather triggers. Such products should enhance, not replace, sound project design. The goal is not to provide insurance for inadequate infrastructure but to make resilience a visible and economically viable priority. “The next phase will reward resilience .” As we reflect on India’s renewable energy achievements, we should focus not only on the gigawatts of capacity added or investments mobilised but also on how reliably that capacity can operate under increasingly volatile conditions. Achieving this requires a closer collaboration among developers, lenders, engineers, insurers, and brokers, ensuring that risk management is as pivotal as technology, costs, and returns.

stories.title: Supreme Court Closes 2021 Plea Seeking Separate Medical Boards For Pregnancy Termination Cases Arising From Rape By Blood Relatives

event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
article_sentences: The Supreme Court recently disposed of a 2021 writ petition seeking constitution of separate Medical Boards across India to decide medical termination of pregnancy cases involving rape by blood relatives.

A bench of CJI Surya Kant, Justice Joymalya Bagchi and Justice V Mohana was dealing with a petition filed seeking primarily two reliefs - (i) permission for medical termination of pregnancy of a 14-year old rape victim, and (ii) direction for Union to frame guidelines constituting qualified Medical Boards in all States/UTs to decide MTP cases beyond 20 weeks of pregnancy, especially in cases of rape by blood relatives.
It is pertinent to note that in a case of rape by blood relative, there is a heightened risk of fetal abnormality.
During the hearing, Advocate VK Biju, for petitioner, contended that the issue was crucial for the SC/ST community, poor and illiterate people.
ASG Aishwarya Bhati informed the Court that after notice was issued in the matter, limited to prayer (ii), the MTP Act and relevant Rules were amended in 2021.
Considering the submission, the Court hoped that the prayer in the writ petition had been suitably addressed.
It observed that the issue whether the amendments have been effective, or the victims continue to face hardships due to prescribed time limits, must be determined on a case-to-case basis.
At last, the Court gave the liberty to file an appropriate petition in case any such case of an aggrieved person comes to notice.

article_sentences: Indian government bonds were little changed on Monday after edging lower at the open, as traders awaited moves in oil prices ahead of an expected U.S. announcement on additional sanctions against Iran.
The yield on the benchmark 6.94 per cent 2036 bond was at 6.8595 per cent as of 10:00 a.m. IST, after closing at 6.8495 per cent on Friday.
The yield posted its biggest weekly rise of the financial year last week.
Indian debt markets are shut on Wednesday for a local holiday.
"We expect to hold current levels for the rest of the day.
Our next move will depend on whether crude prices head toward $90 or $100 a barrel," said a trader at a primary dealership.
The US Treasury Secretary is scheduled to brief media later in the day after warning that Washington could impose "the toughest sanctions in history" on Iran.
President Donald Trump has also threatened sanctions against countries that continue to trade with Tehran.
Iran has denounced the planned US measures, while calling out for a diplomatic resolution.
The benchmark Brent crude held above $92 a barrel, heightening concerns for major oil importers such as India.
Elevated crude prices could stoke inflation, widen the current account deficit and add pressure on government finances.

The minutes of the Reserve Bank of India's August policy meeting published last week, showed that policymakers remain open to raising interest rates if inflationary pressures emerge and become more broad-based.
